items.title: Generative AI chatbot and maternal health outcomes: randomized clinical trial
items.excerpt: In a 400-person RCT across 49 US states, a generative AI maternal health chatbot did not improve 12-month anxiety, depression, ED visits or postpartum care. Pregnant users self-reported more complications in a secondary analysis.
items.rationale: A rare randomized trial of a patient-facing generative AI chatbot, with a null result that matters for anyone deploying chatbots to patients.

items.title: Mayo Clinic Platform launches AI clinical decision support solution integrated into EHRs
items.excerpt: Starting November 2026, Mayo clinicians and partner organizations get an LLM-powered specialty chat covering 35+ specialties, which cites peer-reviewed literature and is updated daily, plus 22 clinical calculators available by chat or voice, embedded in EHR workflows.
items.rationale: A primary-source launch of a clinical decision support tool that goes live inside the EHR workflows of Mayo and its partners this month.

items.title: Google shares its framework for evaluating health AI at scale
items.excerpt: Google published the multi-method evaluation framework it uses to test health AI for safety and helpfulness before and after release, combining automated benchmarks, clinician rating and real-world monitoring.
items.rationale: A major vendor publishes its pre- and post-release health AI safety evaluation method, a concrete reference for clinicians and health systems vetting AI tools.

items.title: External validation of a machine learning model for delirium risk in live clinical practice
items.excerpt: A multimodal NLP delirium-risk model in live use at Mount Sinai was externally validated across hospitals in 33,095 non-ICU admissions. An accompanying commentary covers what implementing it in practice takes beyond discrimination.
items.rationale: External validation of a deployed bedside risk model across hospitals: real patients, real workflow, a specific condition.

items.title: Physical limits to AI substitution across physician specialties
items.excerpt: AI can interpret images, draft assessments and talk with patients, but software cannot examine, biopsy or operate. This NEJM AI analysis maps how exposed each specialty is to AI substitution once physical tasks are counted.
items.rationale: A specialty-by-specialty map of which physician work AI can and cannot absorb, a fresh workforce lens from a top-tier journal.
